question: Why is caregiver training a crucial part of the discharge process in rehab?

options.A: It replaces the need for home health nursing visits.
options.B: It allows the hospital to discharge nursing staff members.
options.C: It ensures family members can safely assist with daily transfers and care at home.
options.D: It legally transfers hospital liability entirely to the family members.

explanation: Well done! Families need hands-on practice in a safe setting so they can care for their loved one at home without hurting themselves or the patient.

question: What did Hippocrates mean when he famously said, 'Let food be thy medicine'?

options.A: Food has no actual impact on human health
options.B: Patients should take drugs instead of eating meals
options.C: Only doctors are allowed to prepare daily meals
options.D: Diet plays a direct role in preventing and treating illness

explanation: Spot on! Hippocrates understood early on that what we eat directly shapes our health and healing journey.

question: A nurse is teaching a parent how to help their child complete homework without getting overwhelmed. What strategy is best to recommend?

options.A: Force the child to finish everything in one long session
options.B: Break large assignments into smaller, manageable steps
options.C: Ignore the homework struggles so the child learns independently
options.D: Punish the child whenever a mistake is made on paper

explanation: Breaking tasks down reduces cognitive overload and anxiety for children who struggle with processing large amounts of information. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h6)

question: How can community leaders help improve low immunization uptake in rural areas?

options.A: By importing vaccines directly from international manufacturers
options.B: By taking over clinical duties and injecting vaccines themselves
options.C: By replacing the cold chain refrigerators with local coolers
options.D: By building trust and addressing local rumors or hesitancy

explanation: Local chiefs and religious leaders have powerful voices. When they support immunization, community members feel much more confident bringing their babies in.

question: As a nurse, why do you collect culture and sensitivity samples?

options.A: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature rapidly
options.B: To stimulate white blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.C: To flush toxic metabolic waste products out of the blood
options.D: To identify the specific pathogen and its drug susceptibilities

explanation: C&S tests help us pinpoint the exact germ causing trouble and find out which specific antibiotic will knock it out.

question: You see a sudden, sharp spike on a monthly infection rate graph that is normally very flat. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The normal daily fluctuation of a healthy patient
options.B: An isolated event, outbreak, or possible data recording error
options.C: A permanent and irreversible change in hospital policy
options.D: The complete eradication of the infectious disease

explanation: Spot on! Sudden peaks jump out because they don't fit the normal pattern—usually pointing to an outbreak or a quick typo in the log.

question: What happens to total maternal serum calcium levels during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: They decrease due to hemodilution and lower albumin
options.B: They increase significantly to support fetal bone growth
options.C: They remain completely unchanged throughout all trimesters
options.D: They drop dangerously low because of kidney failure

explanation: Total serum calcium drops because blood volume expands and blood protein levels fall, but ionized calcium stays normal. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h3)

question: What does it mean when a disease is described as 'endemic' in a community?

options.A: It only affects travellers visiting from foreign countries
options.B: It appears once every ten years and then vanishes
options.C: It is constantly present at a steady baseline level
options.D: It suddenly affects people across multiple continents

explanation: Think of an endemic disease as a constant visitor—it stays within a specific area consistently over time without needing a fresh introduction from outside. You've got this!

question: How does viewing the family as the unit of care change your daily practice as a nurse?

options.A: You avoid giving individual medications to teenagers
options.B: You focus exclusively on genetic disorders during visits
options.C: You spend most of your shift counseling only the head of the household
options.D: You look beyond the sick patient to consider their home support and environment

explanation: Spotting home support and barriers helps you understand why a treatment plan might succeed or struggle at home.

question: Which of the following is considered a consumable medical supply?

options.A: An overhead patient bed
options.B: A mercury sphygmomanometer
options.C: A hospital wheelchair
options.D: Disposable syringes

explanation: Consumables are single-use items that get thrown away after one application, like syringes and gauze. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h2)

question: During normal digestion, what is the main job of the large intestine?

options.A: Breaking down complex proteins into simple amino acids
options.B: Producing bile acids needed for fat digestion
options.C: Absorbing water and electrolytes from waste material
options.D: Secreting large amounts of digestive enzymes into chyme

explanation: Great job! As food waste travels through the colon, the large intestine's primary task is to pull water and minerals back into the body.

question: What is the main class of medications used first-line to treat common intestinal roundworms?

options.A: Benzimidazoles
options.B: Broad-spectrum penicillins
options.C: Loop diuretics
options.D: Antifungal azoles

explanation: Drugs like albendazole and mebendazole belong to the benzimidazole family and are fantastic at clearing out common intestinal worms.

question: A nurse leader wants to assess the prevalence of needle-stick injuries among nurses in a state hospital to justify safety equipment purchases. Which study design is most appropriate?

options.A: Cross-sectional study
options.B: Case report of a single patient
options.C: Laboratory experiment on bacteria cultures
options.D: Retrospective drug trial over ten years

explanation: Spot on! A cross-sectional survey will quickly reveal how common needle-stick injuries are right now, giving solid proof to demand better safety gear.

question: What is the best way to give nutrition advice to teenage girls in a local community?

options.A: Tell them to stop eating all local carbohydrates right away
options.B: Insist they buy expensive imported vitamin pills from the pharmacy
options.C: Hand them strict foreign meal plans they can't find in local markets
options.D: Recommend affordable local foods that fit their culture and daily life

explanation: Wonderful! Advice works best when it uses cheap, familiar local ingredients that families can easily find, afford, and cook.

question: What causes sudden mood swings or impulsive behavior in patients with inherited brain degeneration?

options.A: A deliberate choice by the patient to worry their family members
options.B: An allergic reaction to routine hospital food and noisy wards
options.C: A temporary lack of vitamins due to poor daily eating habits
options.D: Damage to specific brain circuits that normally filter thoughts and impulses

explanation: Great job thinking through this. When the brain's physical filter systems break down, patients lose the ability to easily hold back sudden urges or emotions. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h2)

question: A patient says their knee makes a grating sound when they bend it. What medical term describes this?

options.A: Synovitis
options.B: Ankylosis
options.C: Crepitus
options.D: Osteophytes

explanation: You nailed it! Crepitus is just the clinical word for that crunching or grating feeling when rough bone ends rub against each other.

question: Which imaging test is the gold standard for catching a bone infection early?

options.A: Routine superficial ultrasound
options.B: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
options.C: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
options.D: Standard plain radiography (X-ray)

explanation: X-rays take a while to show bone changes, but an MRI can spot early bone marrow changes and swelling super fast!

question: Which group of medications is commonly used as a short-term fix to manage annoying bleeding caused by progestin implants?

options.A: Strong narcotic pain relievers
options.B: Intravenous general anesthetics
options.C: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
options.D: Inhaled bronchodilator aerosols

explanation: A short course of NSAIDs like ibuprofen can work wonders in calming down irregular or heavy spotting linked to progestin implants.

question: Which workplace factor makes it hardest for employees to bring home-cooked food to their shift?

options.A: Lack of basic amenities like refrigerators and microwaves
options.B: The high cost of buying lunchboxes and food containers
options.C: Mandatory breaks that last less than two minutes
options.D: Company rules that forbid eating food brought from home

explanation: Without a safe place to store and heat food at work, employees have no choice but to buy outside meals or snack on dry foods. You're learning fast!

question: What does the SBAR acronym stand for during a patient handover?

options.A: Symptoms, Breathing, Activity, Recovery
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Safety, Blood, Airway, Respiration
options.D: Staff, Beds, Ambulances, Reports

explanation: Easy peasy! SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation. It keeps your shift handovers clear and professional.

question: How was traditional West African pharmacological knowledge primarily preserved and transmitted?

options.A: Through oral tradition passed down generations
options.B: Through printed textbooks distributed to apprentices
options.C: Via ancient stone tablets stored in royal palaces
options.D: Via detailed digital databases kept by village elders

explanation: Indigenous medicinal knowledge in West Africa was historically preserved and handed down by word of mouth from older healers to younger apprentices. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h2)

question: At what time of day is a blood test most accurate for checking testosterone levels?

options.A: Right before bedtime
options.B: Late afternoon
options.C: Immediately after a heavy meal
options.D: Early morning

explanation: Testosterone levels naturally peak in the early morning hours, so doctors prefer drawing blood then for the most reliable results.

question: Where can polyvalent nurses put their skills to work?

options.A: Solely in out-patient community pharmacies
options.B: Only within government-run research laboratories
options.C: Across various urban and rural health facilities
options.D: Exclusively in private intensive care units

explanation: You nailed it! Because they are so adaptable, polyvalent nurses can fit right into almost any healthcare setting, from city hospitals to village clinics.

question: Which condition is the most common immediate complication following a thoracocentesis?

options.A: Acute liver damage
options.B: Pneumothorax
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Severe kidney failure

explanation: Accidental puncture of the lung surface allows air to enter the pleural space, resulting in a pneumothorax. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h7)

question: What measure helps nurses see the actual size or practical importance of a treatment's effect?

options.A: Sample variance
options.B: Effect size
options.C: P-value
options.D: Null hypothesis

explanation: That's correct! Effect size tells you the actual magnitude of the change, helping you decide if the treatment is powerful enough to matter at the bedside. Great job!

question: A 15-year-old is brought to the accident and emergency unit after falling off the roof of a commercial bus. How is this injury classified?

options.A: Occupational hazard
options.B: Unintentional injury
options.C: Interpersonal violence
options.D: Intentional self-harm

explanation: Spot on! Falling from a moving vehicle without any intent to harm oneself or others is classified as an unintentional injury.

question: What are the two main mechanisms that move an egg through the fallopian tube?

options.A: Blood pressure and gravity
options.B: Ligament pulling and fluid diffusion
options.C: Cilia sweeping and muscular peristalsis
options.D: Ovarian suction and uterine contractions

explanation: Hair-like cilia on the lining cells and wave-like muscle contractions work together to push the egg along. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h2)

question: How does psychoeducation benefit families of clients with mental health conditions?

options.A: It legally transfers all medical responsibility away from the healthcare team
options.B: It empowers them with knowledge about the illness and how to handle crises effectively
options.C: It completely eliminates all stressful events from their household
options.D: It teaches them how to diagnose and prescribe psychiatric drugs independently

explanation: When families understand the condition and recognize early warning signs, they can provide supportive care and prevent emergency situations. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: A patient has Type A blood. What type of antibodies circulate in their plasma?

options.A: No antibodies at all
options.B: Anti-A antibodies
options.C: Anti-B antibodies
options.D: Both anti-A and anti-B antibodies

explanation: People with Type A blood have A antigens on their cells, so their immune system develops anti-B antibodies to fight off foreign B-type blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which behavior is a clear sign of medication non-adherence?

options.A: Asking the pharmacist about the cost of a new drug
options.B: Taking a morning pill one hour earlier than usual
options.C: Reporting a mild side effect to the attending nurse
options.D: Stopping a blood pressure pill because the patient feels better

explanation: Stopping medication simply because symptoms disappear shows a lack of adherence to the long-term treatment plan. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: Which skin problem happens most often when urinary incontinence is left untreated?

options.A: Deep pressure ulcers over the shoulder blades
options.B: Dry, scaly skin patches across the upper arms
options.C: Perineal dermatitis and breakdown from moisture
options.D: Fungal rashes spreading across the face and chest

explanation: When skin stays in contact with urine too long, the moisture breaks down the skin barrier and causes painful irritation or rashes.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge in disease surveillance?

options.A: Fear of social stigma and discrimination in communities
options.B: An overabundance of fully trained staff and limitless financial funding
options.C: Poor infrastructure like unreliable internet and transport
options.D: Underreporting of cases by busy or overworked clinical staff

explanation: If only we had endless money and staff! In reality, health systems always struggle with shortages, not an overabundance of funding.

question: A patient living near farm animals comes in with a suspected zoonotic infection. What is the best health advice to give them?

options.A: Tell them never to take medications for animal scratches
options.B: Suggest getting rid of every single animal in the neighborhood
options.C: Teach them safe food handling and how to protect themselves around animals
options.D: Tell them humans only catch things from other humans

explanation: Good hygiene, safe food prep, and protective gear go a long way in keeping animal germs away from humans.

question: What type of medication must be given for a few weeks before surgery to remove a pheochromocytoma?

options.A: Alpha-blockers
options.B: Potassium supplements
options.C: Insulin infusions
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Before surgeons touch a pheochromocytoma, the patient needs alpha-blockers to keep their blood vessels relaxed and prevent dangerous blood pressure spikes during the operation.

question: A patient having a severe allergic reaction has wheezing, swollen lips, and crashing blood pressure. What medication is given first?

options.A: Intramuscular epinephrine
options.B: Oral diphenhydramine
options.C: Subcutaneous insulin
options.D: Intravenous paracetamol

explanation: Brilliant! Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis because it quickly opens up the airways and brings blood pressure back up.

question: Why does a requisition form need a supervisor's review and signature before heading to the store?

options.A: To stop nurses from talking to warehouse workers
options.B: To delay delivery and keep storerooms empty
options.C: To give the medical director extra paperwork to sign
options.D: To confirm that what you asked for matches your actual usage

explanation: Exactly! Authorization checks help catch mistakes, prevent over-ordering, and keep everything transparent.

question: What is a major risk for low-income families trying to pay for long-term home nursing care?

options.A: Mandatory relocation to a tertiary hospital
options.B: Severe financial strain and potential impoverishment
options.C: Immediate access to free government medications
options.D: Automatic enrollment in private insurance plans

explanation: That's right! Paying private nurses out of pocket for a long time can drain a family's savings very quickly.

question: Why should nurses be careful about relying solely on intuition for patient care?

options.A: It always leads to incorrect clinical decisions
options.B: It is subjective, hard to explain, and prone to personal bias
options.C: It only works for surgical nurses and never for public health nurses
options.D: It is illegal to document gut feelings on a patient chart

explanation: Gut feelings can give you a helpful warning, but they need to be backed up by real, measurable patient assessments.

question: What is the main purpose of taking mental health care out into the community?

options.A: To replace all general hospitals with psychiatric units
options.B: To force patients into long-term institutional confinement
options.C: To eliminate the need for any trained medical personnel
options.D: To shift mental health care closer to people's living spaces and reduce stigma

explanation: Bringing care to the community makes it friendly, accessible, and helps chase away the fear and stigma attached to mental illness.

question: What is the primary purpose of communication in nursing practice?

options.A: To share information safely
options.B: To fill out hospital paperwork
options.C: To pass time during shifts
options.D: To impress attending doctors

explanation: Effective sharing of information prevents errors and protects patient safety during care delivery. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h1)

question: A nurse is writing an introduction for a study on hand hygiene. What is the main goal of this section?

options.A: Summarizing the final statistical data collected from the hospital wards
options.B: Establishing the gap in current compliance knowledge and stating study aims
options.C: Providing personal opinions on why hospital staff refuse to wash hands
options.D: Listing every historical discovery of microscopic bacteria since the nineteenth century

explanation: The introduction sets the stage by showing what we already know, what is missing, and why this study is so important.

question: A patient asks why a food with a high glycemic index can sometimes still be eaten in small amounts. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The glycemic index only applies to people who do not take insulin.
options.B: Glycemic load looks at actual portion size, so a small serving has less overall impact.
options.C: Small amounts of high GI foods completely cure insulin resistance.
options.D: High GI foods automatically turn into low GI foods if you chew them slowly.

explanation: Glycemic load combines the GI score with the actual amount of food eaten, giving a realistic picture of blood sugar impact. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: What does it mean when a patient is in a positive energy balance?

options.A: Caloric expenditure is greater than caloric intake
options.B: Total body weight remains completely unchanging
options.C: Caloric intake and expenditure are perfectly equal
options.D: Caloric intake is greater than caloric expenditure

explanation: When you take in more food energy than your body burns, the extra energy is stored. That's a positive energy balance!

question: Who is considered the primary client for a community health nurse?

options.A: The attending physician
options.B: The hospitalized patient
options.C: The local government authority
options.D: The entire community

explanation: Great job thinking big picture! Unlike bedside nursing that focuses on one patient at a time, community health nurses look at the health of the whole population in an area.

question: Which indicator measures the final health results experienced by the patient?

options.A: Outcome indicator
options.B: Financial indicator
options.C: Process indicator
options.D: Structure indicator

explanation: Outcome indicators look at the end result—whether the patient recovered well, had complications, or improved overall.

question: A mother asks which local foods she can give her toddler to prevent iron deficiency. What should you recommend?

options.A: Cassava flakes (garri) soaked in plain cold water
options.B: Pure vegetable oil and polished white rice
options.C: White bread, refined sugar, and bottled juices
options.D: Lean meats, liver, beans, and dark green leafy vegetables

explanation: Foods like liver, beans, and local greens (like ugwu) are fantastic, budget-friendly sources of iron to keep little ones strong and energized.

question: Which nursing action is best for keeping track of a patient's ongoing nutrition?

options.A: Prescribing high-protein dietary supplements independently
options.B: Measuring indirect calorimetry on every single shift
options.C: Calculating precise basal metabolic rate without a formula
options.D: Recording daily weights and monitoring food intake

explanation: Never underestimate the basics! Daily weight checks and watching how much food actually gets eaten give nurses the best clues on nutritional health.

question: Which vitamin is especially important for building collagen during long-term wound healing?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin D

explanation: You nailed it! Vitamin C is key for making collagen, which acts like glue to heal surgical cuts.

question: Why do we need to make sure we have enough trained staff before starting a health program?

options.A: To guarantee that administrative tasks take precedence over patient care
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement set by international donor agencies
options.C: To ensure the workforce can handle the service volume without burning out
options.D: To prevent the community from ever questioning clinical decisions

explanation: Matching your team size to the expected crowd keeps patients happy and protects our hardworking nurses from burnout.

question: When is the best time to check back on a patient after giving them oral pain medication?

options.A: Before the next scheduled meal
options.B: Within 30 to 60 minutes
options.C: Immediately upon injection
options.D: After exactly 24 hours

question: In maternal health, what does the 'second delay' usually involve?

options.A: Delays by the government in building enough clinics in urban areas
options.B: Delays by doctors in prescribing the correct antibiotics during labor
options.C: Delays in the manufacturing of essential maternity drugs and supplies
options.D: Delays in reaching a medical facility due to transportation or household power dynamics

explanation: The second delay is all about the journey to the hospital. It drags out when a pregnant woman has to wait for transport money or permission from family members.

question: Why should you tell a patient to avoid clearing their throat aggressively right after a laryngoscopy?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from writing the final discharge summary.
options.B: It increases the patient's blood pressure and heart rate significantly.
options.C: It forces the residual topical spray down into the stomach too fast.
options.D: It can cause trauma or irritation to the recently numbed vocal cords.

explanation: Spot on! Since the vocal cords are still a bit sleepy and vulnerable, harsh throat clearing can easily bruise or injure them.

question: Why is the nurse's role so crucial for making a National Drug Policy work in real life?

options.A: Nurses are solely responsible for importing essential medicines from international manufacturers.
options.B: Nurses are the frontline professionals who handle, administer, and educate patients about medications daily.
options.C: Nurses hold the legal authority to shut down illegal open-air drug markets across the country.
options.D: Nurses write the legal statutes that govern pharmaceutical practice in government courts.

explanation: Policies are just paper until we put them into practice! Because nurses handle, give, and teach about drugs every day, our actions make the policy a success.

question: How do qualitative and quantitative approaches differ in their main goals?

options.A: Qualitative avoids human subjects while quantitative studies only animals
options.B: Qualitative uses statistical formulas while quantitative uses personal stories
options.C: Qualitative focuses on lab equipment while quantitative focuses on interviews
options.D: Qualitative seeks deep meaning while quantitative seeks prediction and control

explanation: Simply put: qualitative wants to understand the 'why' and 'how' of feelings, while quantitative wants to measure and test facts.

question: What is a pathologic fracture?

options.A: A break occurring in a bone weakened by an underlying disease
options.B: A minor hairline crack caused by repetitive athletic training
options.C: A clean break resulting from a high-speed motor vehicle crash
options.D: A fracture caused strictly by a direct blow from a blunt object

explanation: Pathologic fractures happen because an existing disease like cancer or osteoporosis has already made the bone fragile. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h2)

question: What does a simple frequency distribution table show us?

options.A: A map of hospital departments
options.B: The exact daily schedule of clinical staff
options.C: The financial budget of a hospital ward
options.D: How often specific values or categories occur

explanation: A frequency table simply counts and shows how many times a particular observation or response pops up in your data.

question: Why do you need to act immediately when a patient gets a chemical splash in the eye?

options.A: Chemicals quickly burn and damage delicate eye tissues
options.B: Waiting prevents the nurse from finding a neutralizing agent
options.C: Delayed washing allows the chemical to crystallize into a solid
options.D: Chemical splashes rapidly lower the normal body temperature

explanation: Time is precious here! Harsh substances start destroying eye cells right away, so washing them out fast stops permanent injury.

question: Which action represents effective nursing advocacy in food policy?

options.A: Personally financing the national agricultural subsidy budget
options.B: Sharing clinical data with policymakers to support nutritional programs
options.C: Refusing to care for patients who eat unhealthy processed foods
options.D: Replacing all government food inspectors with hospital nurses

explanation: Nurses use their clinical insights to influence decision-makers and support programs that improve community health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: Which of these actions is an example of professional negligence?

options.A: Reporting a faulty infusion pump to the biomedical engineering department
options.B: Asking a patient to explain their understanding of a surgical procedure
options.C: Failing to check a patient blood pressure before giving a blood pressure medication
options.D: Refusing to participate in an unethical research study on patients

explanation: Great job! Giving a blood pressure medication without checking if their BP is already too low is a dangerous slip in the standard of care.

question: What is a common challenge that QA committees face in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Excessive funding that makes budget management difficult
options.B: Too much free time for clinical staff during working hours
options.C: Having way too many medical doctors and nurses in every ward
options.D: Severe staff shortages and heavy workloads leading to fatigue

explanation: True indeed! Manpower shortages and burnout are everyday hurdles our healthcare system works hard to manage.

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in your daily clinical practice?

options.A: Administering medication without causing harm to patients or yourself
options.B: Using only intravenous routes for fluid replacement
options.C: Ensuring every patient gets at least one daily injection
options.D: Disposing of all used syringes in household trash bins

explanation: You've got this! Injection safety is all about protecting everyone—patients, healthcare workers, and the community—from any harm related to injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why must clinic nurses report unusual or severe side effects (AEFIs) to health authorities?

options.A: To punish the community health worker who administered the injection
options.B: To stop mothers from bringing their babies for future visits
options.C: To investigate vaccine safety and maintain public trust in the program
options.D: To immediately ban all vaccine manufacturing in the country

explanation: Exactly right! Reporting helps health teams track safety, catch batch issues early, and keep parents confident in immunizations.

question: Why does sensorineural hearing loss often make speech sound muffled instead of just quiet?

options.A: Excess earwax completely fills the inner ear chambers
options.B: The middle ear bones fuse together to block high pitches
options.C: The eardrum becomes too thick to vibrate at any frequency
options.D: Inner ear damage alters how sound clarity and frequencies are processed

explanation: Great job thinking this through! When the inner ear or auditory nerve gets damaged, it messes up how details and frequencies are sent to the brain, turning clear words into a muffled sound.

question: In public health, what age group is generally referred to as adolescents?

options.A: 20 to 30 years
options.B: 5 to 9 years
options.C: 10 to 19 years
options.D: 35 to 50 years

explanation: Spot on! The World Health Organization defines adolescence as the teenage years spanning from 10 to 19 years of age.

question: A patient sits up on the side of the bed in preparation for walking and immediately reports feeling very dizzy and lightheaded. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Lay the patient back down and postpone ambulation
options.B: Administer a strong pain medication immediately
options.C: Force them to stand up quickly to test their balance
options.D: Leave the room to fetch a wheelchair right away

question: What is the main purpose of competitive bidding when buying DRF supplies?

options.A: To delay the purchasing process until more patients arrive
options.B: To ensure only foreign pharmaceutical companies win contracts
options.C: To secure the best quality drugs at fair and reasonable prices
options.D: To eliminate the need for physical stock verification checks

explanation: Asking multiple suppliers to bid gives the hospital choices, ensuring you get top-quality medicines without getting overcharged.

question: What is the main reason a fecal impaction forms in the rectum?

options.A: Too much nerve stimulation in the lower spinal cord
options.B: Waste sitting in the bowel too long, losing all its water
options.C: Eating way too many high-fiber foods every day

explanation: If stool hangs out in the rectum for too long, the body keeps sucking water out of it until it turns into a hard, stubborn rock-like mass.

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended first step when managing challenging behaviors in dementia?

options.A: Immediate prescription of heavy antipsychotic medications
options.B: Reviewing the daily routine for sources of overstimulation
options.C: Playing soft and familiar background music
options.D: Looking for signs of physical pain or discomfort

explanation: Always start with non-drug approaches! Heavy meds carry serious risks and shouldn't be the first resort for everyday behavioral issues.

question: What is one of the main roles of a community health nurse in an intersectoral team?

options.A: Acting as a bridge connecting community members with other developmental sectors
options.B: Managing hospital budgets for the entire state health ministry
options.C: Taking over the administrative duties of local government chairpersons
options.D: Constructing boreholes and building roads without outside assistance

explanation: Right! Nurses serve as the vital link between health needs and sectors like water, education, and agriculture to solve problems together.

question: How does delaying salary payments during economic hardships affect nurses?

options.A: They have no impact on daily clinical performance
options.B: They encourage nurses to work longer hours with enthusiasm
options.C: They improve interprofessional collaboration within the ward
options.D: They demotivate staff and can trigger industrial strikes

explanation: Unpaid salaries cause real financial stress, lowering morale and sometimes leading to strikes as workers demand what is due.

question: How does the body respond during a negative energy balance?

options.A: It burns stored fat and tissue to meet energy needs.
options.B: It stops all metabolic processes completely.
options.C: It increases total body mass rapidly.
options.D: It stores all incoming nutrients directly as fat.

explanation: When you burn more than you eat, the body cleverly taps into its stored fat and tissues for backup power, leading to weight loss.

question: A patient after cancer surgery refuses to get out of bed to walk. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Allow the patient to stay in bed all day without moving
options.B: Wait until the surgeon arrives before attempting any movement
options.C: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with recovery
options.D: Explain that early walking helps prevent blood clots and lung problems

explanation: Kind patient education works wonders! A gentle explanation helps them see why moving early is vital for preventing serious issues like clots. You've got the nurse's touch!

question: What is a great trick to help a mum manage early morning pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Remaining completely fasting until the afternoon hours
options.B: Eating small, dry carbohydrate snacks before getting out of bed
options.C: Consuming a heavy, high-fat breakfast right away
options.D: Drinking a large cup of cold whole milk immediately upon waking

explanation: Such a classic nursing tip! A dry biscuit before standing up keeps blood sugar stable and calms that empty, nauseous tummy.

question: Which service is especially helpful for giving family caregivers of individuals with ASD a much-needed break?

options.A: Respite care services
options.B: Sudden medication changes
options.C: Mandatory legal arbitration
options.D: Extended hospital admission

explanation: Spot on! Caring for someone full-time is heavy work. Respite care gives families a temporary break to rest and recharge.

question: What is the main reason for doing routine physical stock counts in a pharmacy?

options.A: To compare actual physical inventory with financial records
options.B: To calculate the annual salary bonus for the nursing staff
options.C: To return all expired items directly to government ministers
options.D: To increase the retail price of all fast-moving medications

explanation: Stock counts help catch errors, missing items, or record mistakes early, making sure the physical drugs match what the books say.

question: What do we call 'diagnostic overshadowing' when caring for a patient with a disability?

options.A: Overprescribing pain relief medication for chronic joint stiffness
options.B: Failing to document medical history correctly in the patient chart
options.C: Using outdated diagnostic machinery during routine check-ups
options.D: Attributing all new symptoms mistakenly to the existing disability

explanation: It's a sneaky trap! This happens when we assume a new problem is just 'part of their usual condition' and forget to investigate properly. Always look closer!

question: Why does obstetric fistula often cause women to face social isolation in their communities?

options.A: Patients lose their ability to speak after the injury
options.B: Continuous incontinence leads to severe social stigma and shame
options.C: Government laws require isolation of all surgical patients
options.D: Traditional healers forbid them from leaving their homes

explanation: Because of constant leaking of urine or stool, affected women often face heartbreaking stigma and misunderstanding from their communities. As nurses, our empathy and care are crucial in supporting and healing them.

question: What is the primary advantage of mobile health clinics in reproductive health outreach?

options.A: Providing free cars to every pregnant woman
options.B: Replacing all permanent hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Eliminating the need for community health education
options.D: Bringing family planning supplies directly to remote villages

explanation: Mobile clinics bridge the geographical gap by bringing essential services closer to people who live far from standard health facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: Which measure is best for protecting a DRF from internal fraud and missing stock?

options.A: Allowing pharmacy cashiers to set their own daily mark-up rates
options.B: Keeping all financial records hidden from the hospital management committee
options.C: Implementing regular internal audits and automated inventory tracking
options.D: Relying solely on verbal reports from the procurement officer

explanation: You guessed it! Regular audits and clear digital tracking leave a reliable paper trail, making it much harder for inventory or cash to go missing unnoticed.

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by the sperm normally take place in the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Ampulla
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Cervix
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle section of the fallopian tube, providing just the right space for the sperm to meet and fertilize the egg.

question: A nurse tests a new patient intake form and finds it saves time but needs two small tweaks. What should be done next?

options.A: Adapt the form with the needed tweaks and run another small test
options.B: Abandon all forms and return to chaotic verbal reporting forever
options.C: Punish the nurses for not making the original form perfect
options.D: Adopt the flawed form immediately across the entire national health system

explanation: Spot on! If an idea is almost there, we adapt it with our improvements and give it another quick test.

question: Which member of the healthcare team helps a patient relearn how to swallow safely?

options.A: Clinical Pharmacist
options.B: Physical Therapist
options.C: Speech-Language Pathologist
options.D: Occupational Therapist

explanation: Well done! Speech-Language Pathologists do much more than speech—they are experts in evaluating and treating swallowing difficulties too.

question: When the kidneys secrete hydrogen ions into the urine, what vital body balance are they maintaining?

options.A: Red blood cell production
options.B: Calcium and bone density
options.C: Acid-base balance
options.D: Blood glucose balance

explanation: Correct! Getting rid of excess hydrogen ions helps clear out acid, keeping your blood pH nicely balanced and steady.

question: How does a community health nurse's role differ from a hospital nurse?

options.A: The community nurse has no responsibility for patient health outcomes
options.B: The community nurse spends all shift managing mechanical ventilators
options.C: The community nurse strictly follows rigid hospital visiting rules
options.D: The community nurse focuses more on education, advocacy, and resource linkage

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses shine by teaching populations and connecting families to health resources around them.

question: What is the main difference between decorticate and decerebrate posturing when scoring motor response?

options.A: Decorticate involves abnormal flexion inward, while decerebrate involves rigid extension outward
options.B: Decorticate affects only the legs, while decerebrate affects only the arms
options.C: Decorticate is scored as a 5, while decerebrate is scored as a 4
options.D: Decorticate means the patient obeys commands, while decerebrate means they make no sound

explanation: Think of decorticate (flexion/inward toward the core) scoring a 3, and decerebrate (extension/rigid outward) scoring a 2. Both point to serious brain stress, but knowing the physical posturing helps you chart accurately.

question: A patient asks how Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) works. How should you explain it?

options.A: It builds a chemical defense in your body so the virus cannot establish an infection if you are exposed
options.B: It permanently boosts your natural red blood cell count to fight off germs
options.C: It numbs nerve endings so you no longer feel any pain during intercourse
options.D: It cures any existing HIV infection within the first week of daily dosing

explanation: You got it! PrEP gives the body a protective chemical shield so the virus can't take hold if exposure happens.

question: Which drug combination is a dangerous, strict 'no-go' for an angina patient?

options.A: Nitrates and erectile dysfunction medications
options.B: Calcium channel blockers and mild laxatives
options.C: Nitrates and daily multivitamin supplements
options.D: Beta-blockers and daily low-dose aspirin

explanation: Combining nitrates with ED meds causes a sudden, massive drop in blood pressure that can be life-threatening. Always screen for this!

question: What is the purpose of the 'teach-back' method in home care?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to grade the family's cleaning skills
options.B: Checking if the patient or caregiver truly understands instructions
options.C: Testing the patient's ability to read a textbook out loud
options.D: Teaching the nurse how to use home appliances

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?', you ask them to explain the instructions back to you in their own words. It's a game-changer for safety!

question: What shape is the anterior (front) fontanelle?

options.A: Round-shaped
options.B: Diamond-shaped
options.C: Oval-shaped
options.D: Triangle-shaped

explanation: You got it! The anterior fontanelle sits right at the front and is famously diamond-shaped.

question: Why do women need to use chemical spermicide along with a diaphragm?

options.A: To lubricate the device for easy insertion
options.B: To immobilize and kill sperm that pass the barrier
options.C: To permanently alter the pH of the cervix
options.D: To prevent the growth of yeast infections

explanation: While the physical cup blocks most sperm, spermicide acts as a backup to kill any little swimmers that might slip past the edges!

question: Which of these is a core duty of a psychiatric nurse in an MHPSS team?

options.A: Designing national economic recovery policies
options.B: Managing international humanitarian funding budgets
options.C: Administering and monitoring psychotropic medications
options.D: Conducting major neurosurgeries for brain tumors

explanation: Spot on! Your training prepares you to safely give psychiatric drugs, check for side effects, and see how well the patient is responding.

question: Which part of the inner ear turns sound vibrations into electrical signals for the brain?

options.A: Cochlea
options.B: Tympanic membrane
options.C: Malleus
options.D: Auditory canal

explanation: The cochlea is shaped like a little snail shell. It is packed with fluid and tiny hair cells that translate physical sound waves into nerve impulses.

question: What is a major economic reason why impoverished households practice child marriage?

options.A: Complying with mandatory government taxation policies for unmarried girls
options.B: Securing high-paying white-collar employment for the young bride
options.C: Funding the higher education of male siblings in the family
options.D: Reducing household financial burdens through bride price or fewer dependents

explanation: Extreme poverty pushes some families to marry off young daughters to ease household expenses and sometimes gain financial help through bride wealth.

question: What do we mean when we talk about a patient's 'health literacy'?

options.A: The capacity to process and understand basic health information
options.B: The speed at which a patient can swallow multiple tablets
options.C: The total number of years a patient spent in formal education
options.D: The ability to read advanced medical textbooks and journals

explanation: Health literacy is simply how well someone can understand basic health info to make good choices about their body and care. You've got this!

question: Why does milk production stop when a baby is abruptly weaned?

options.A: The posterior pituitary gland permanently stops producing oxytocin stores.
options.B: Circulating levels of maternal estrogen drop to zero within twenty-four hours.
options.C: Accumulated milk triggers feedback inhibitors that signal secretory cells to halt production.
options.D: The lactiferous sinuses permanently fuse shut due to lack of use.

explanation: When milk sits in the breast and isn't removed, it creates pressure and releases a special chemical signal that tells the cells, 'Stop making more, we're full!'

question: How does lowering dietary protein help a patient with severe liver failure?

options.A: It prevents a dangerous buildup of toxic ammonia in the blood
options.B: It lowers the patient's blood pressure back to normal
options.C: It allows the liver to regenerate new cells overnight
options.D: It stops internal bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: A failing liver cannot process ammonia properly, so reducing dietary protein lowers the amount of ammonia produced in the gut. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h2)

question: What is the best bed position to set a patient in before you feed them?

options.A: 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 30 degrees
options.D: 15 degrees

explanation: Sitting them straight up (High Fowler's at 90 degrees) lets gravity do the hard work, pulling food safely down the esophagus instead of toward the airway.

question: Why must different sectors work together during a major disaster?

options.A: Private businesses are legally required to manage all health emergencies
options.B: International law strictly forbids any single organization from responding alone
options.C: Government ministries refuse to release funds unless outside groups help
options.D: No single agency has all the total capacity, funding, and personnel needed

explanation: Big disasters are too much for just one group. Working together makes sure no important tasks get left behind!

question: Why is continuous electronic fetal monitoring so important during preterm labour?

options.A: Preterm fetuses tolerate the stress of contractions poorly
options.B: It stops the progress of cervical dilation automatically
options.C: It is the only way to calculate the exact due date
options.D: It prevents the mother from experiencing any back pain

explanation: Preterm babies have delicate reserves, so watching the monitor closely helps us catch signs of distress early. You're learning top-tier patient safety!

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main roles when it comes to nutrition and diet therapy?

options.A: Translating nutrition therapy into practical everyday habits for patients
options.B: Writing the definitive medical nutrition prescription for the hospital kitchen
options.C: Designing institutional food service menus for surgical wards
options.D: Diagnosing rare nutritional deficiencies using laboratory blood work

explanation: You are the vital link between doctor's orders and real life! Your job is to help patients take clinical nutrition advice and fit it smoothly into their daily meals and lifestyle.

question: What is the main benefit of pursed-lip breathing for a patient with chronic breathing difficulties?

options.A: It stops the heart from beating too fast during movement
options.B: It keeps airways open longer by creating gentle back-pressure during exhalation
options.C: It forces all the air out of the lungs in a single quick second
options.D: It pumps extra water vapor directly into the stomach lining

explanation: Breathing out through pursed lips creates small back-pressure that stops fragile airways from collapsing too early during exhalation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h6)

question: What key feature is always present in a true experiment, but often missing in a quasi-experiment?

options.A: Formulation of a clear research question
options.B: Measurement of dependent variables
options.C: Review by an ethics committee
options.D: Random assignment of subjects to groups

explanation: You nailed it. True experiments randomly toss participants into groups to keep things fair and balanced.

question: In microbiology, what is the main purpose of 'nomenclature'?

options.A: Measuring physical cell size
options.B: Determining antibiotic resistance
options.C: Assigning formal scientific names
options.D: Observing metabolic heat output

explanation: Think of nomenclature as giving official names to microorganisms using established rules, just like giving every newborn a proper name!

question: Which group is considered especially vulnerable in community health?

options.A: Wealthy urban property owners
options.B: Children under five years old
options.C: Employed corporate executives
options.D: Licensed medical practitioners

explanation: Great job! Under-fives are easily affected by infections and poor nutrition, making them a key focus for public health nurses.

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to prescribe antibiotics along with draining an abscess?

options.A: The presence of severe surrounding skin redness and swelling
options.B: The patient developing a fever and systemic chills
options.C: The patient simply prefers taking pills over wound care
options.D: The patient having a compromised immune system

explanation: Antibiotics are powerful drugs reserved for spreading infections, fevers, or weak immune systems—never just because a patient prefers taking pills over doing proper wound care.

question: Why is the biopsychosocial model especially useful in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It helps nurses look at the whole person rather than just one symptom
options.B: It ensures that every patient receives the exact same treatment plan
options.C: It replaces the need for any laboratory testing or physical exams
options.D: It proves that all mental illnesses are caused by bad parenting

explanation: Because mental disorders have multiple roots, this model encourages nurses to assess physical, emotional, and social aspects of a patient's life for holistic care. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why must instrument packs inside an autoclave chamber be loosely arranged rather than tightly packed?

options.A: Loose packs dry much faster after the cycle ends
options.B: Tightly packed metal will melt from the intense heat
options.C: Air pockets help the machine reach high pressure quicker
options.D: Steam must circulate freely around every item

explanation: If packs are squeezed together, steam cannot penetrate the center, leaving some instruments unsterilized. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: If a patient suffers a ruptured ectopic pregnancy, what main substance builds up in her Pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Blood
options.C: Lymph fluid
options.D: Urine

explanation: Spot on! A tubal rupture causes internal bleeding, and since blood is a heavy fluid, it flows down to collect in that lowest pelvic space.

question: Why is getting a detailed witness account so important when assessing a patient with a suspected paroxysmal disorder?

options.A: Witnesses can accurately measure the exact brain wave frequency.
options.B: Doctors rely on family members to prescribe the correct medication.
options.C: Patients often have no memory of the actual event.
options.D: Patients always exaggerate their physical symptoms during attacks.

explanation: Because altered awareness or unconsciousness is common during seizures, bystanders provide the most reliable description of what happened. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h5)

question: What are the four main steps food goes through from the farm to your plate?

options.A: Importing, exporting, taxing, and selling
options.B: Storage, cooking, eating, and waste disposal
options.C: Planting, watering, weeding, and harvesting
options.D: Production, processing, distribution, and consumption

explanation: Think of food's journey: it is first grown (production), packaged or altered (processing), moved to stores (distribution), and finally eaten (consumption). Easy to remember!

question: Why is teamwork (multidisciplinary approach) so important for an abused child's long-term care?

options.A: Child protection laws prohibit nurses from working independently
options.B: Social workers require medical doctors to handle foster placements
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to document clinical findings
options.D: Different specialists address medical, legal, and psychological needs

explanation: Abuse affects every part of a child's life. Nurses, social workers, doctors, and police all have to team up to help.

question: During early blood loss, what is the body's main goal to protect itself?

options.A: Slower heart rate to save energy
options.B: Increase urine production to flush toxins
options.C: Maintain blood supply to the brain and heart
options.D: Keep the skin warm and well-perfused

explanation: In early shock, the body smartly shunts blood away from less critical areas to protect VIP organs like the brain and heart.

question: Which of these items is counted as a medical sharp?

options.A: Plastic medication cup
options.B: Rubber tourniquet
options.C: Disposable surgical blade
options.D: Cotton wool pledget

explanation: Surgical blades have sharp edges that can easily cut human skin, so they belong in the sharps box.

question: A nurse is assigned to visit a new patient in an unfamiliar, isolated neighborhood. What major safety risk must they consider?

options.A: Strict penalties from the national health insurance board
options.B: Immediate termination of nursing license for home visits
options.C: Mandatory participation in local cultural festivals
options.D: Exposure to security threats like robbery or assault

explanation: Correct! Stepping into unknown neighborhoods always means keeping your personal safety and security in mind.

question: Why is a previous classical cesarean section a strong contraindication for home delivery?

options.A: The baby will automatically be born too early
options.B: It causes the mother to lose her voice during contractions
options.C: Stitches from the old operation will make the baby cold
options.D: There is a high risk of uterine rupture during labor

explanation: A scarred uterus can tear open under the pressure of strong contractions, which is a life-threatening emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why are fat-soluble vitamin supplements more likely to cause toxicity than water-soluble ones?

options.A: They are much stronger chemically than water-soluble vitamins and minerals.
options.B: The human liver cannot break them down into less harmful waste products.
options.C: They are stored in body fat and the liver instead of being flushed out in urine.
options.D: They directly destroy the mucosal lining of the stomach when swallowed.

explanation: Because your body holds onto fat-soluble vitamins instead of washing them away, taking too many supplements over time lets them build up to dangerous levels. Moderation is key!

question: What key physical features must a proper sharps container have?

options.A: Transparent and open at the top
options.B: Biodegradable and water-soluble
options.C: Puncture-resistant and leak-proof
options.D: Made of soft, flexible cardboard

explanation: Sharps bins have to be tough! Being puncture-resistant and leak-proof ensures that needles won't poke through and fluids won't spill out while waiting for disposal.

question: Why do nurses document patient care?

options.A: To prove the nurse worked a full shift
options.B: To provide data for hospital billing only
options.C: To replace verbal handovers entirely
options.D: To communicate care among the healthcare team

explanation: Great job! Writing things down ensures doctors, nurses on other shifts, and therapists all know what is happening with your patient.

question: When it comes to formatting your paper, what golden rule connects your in-text citations and reference list?

options.A: Every in-text citation must match an entry in the reference list
options.B: Only textbooks published before the year 2000 need to be referenced
options.C: References must be completely different from the in-text citations
options.D: References should be listed in alphabetical order without citations

explanation: Good academic practice means if you cite someone in your paragraph, their full details must show up in your reference list at the end. No missing links!

question: What makes a conceptual framework so useful when you are reading a published nursing study?

options.A: It proves the researcher spent a lot of money on the project
options.B: It lists every single patient who refused to participate
options.C: It makes the study goals and variable relationships instantly clear
options.D: It replaces the abstract and the conclusion sections

explanation: A good diagram or framework gives you a quick snapshot so you can understand the whole study at a single glance.

question: What is the primary receptor targeted by Class II antiarrhythmic drugs?

options.A: Calcium binding sites
options.B: Potassium ion channels
options.C: Beta-adrenergic receptors
options.D: Sodium transport gates

explanation: Class II drugs are beta-blockers that attach to beta-adrenergic receptors to block the effects of adrenaline on the heart. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h4)

question: When is a nurse legally and ethically allowed to break an adolescent's confidentiality?

options.A: Whenever the teenager admits to eating junk food at school
options.B: When there is a clear danger of severe abuse or self-harm
options.C: Whenever a parent asks what happened during the consultation
options.D: When the adolescent misses a scheduled follow-up appointment

explanation: Confidentiality must be broken only when the physical safety and immediate welfare of the young person are seriously threatened. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h4)

question: What do we mean by a "learning experience" in your nursing training?

options.A: The formal evaluation score recorded by a clinical preceptor
options.B: A lecture delivered strictly inside a university auditorium
options.C: Any activity or interaction that helps you build knowledge and skills
options.D: A written examination given at the end of a clinical rotation

explanation: Think of a learning experience as any moment—whether in class, lab, or the ward—that helps you grow your professional skills. You've got this!

question: A farmer arrives at the clinic with severe muscle twitching and too much saliva after working in the fields. What caused this?

options.A: A natural disaster caused by flooding
options.B: A chemical exposure from pesticides
options.C: A traumatic injury from a falling tree branch
options.D: A biological outbreak of meningitis

explanation: Pesticides are powerful chemicals that affect the nervous system, leading to symptoms like twitching and excess saliva. You're learning fast!

question: What critical allergy information must you check before giving any new drug?

options.A: Favorite foods and dietary preferences
options.B: Known drug allergies and past adverse reactions
options.C: Family history of seasonal pollen allergies
options.D: Reactions to household cleaning supplies

explanation: Always ask about past drug reactions! It's a quick question that protects your patient from severe allergic responses like anaphylaxis.

question: When giving the BCG vaccine to a newborn, which injection route and technique should you use?

options.A: Deep intramuscular injection at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Oral drops placed directly onto the tongue
options.C: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty thigh tissue
options.D: Intradermal injection forming a small skin bleb

explanation: You'll practice this a lot in clinic! BCG goes right into the top layer of skin (intradermal), which raises a nice little skin bleb.

question: Which of these crops make up the traditional, local staple foods in Nigerian diets?

options.A: Imported canned beef and biscuits
options.B: Yams, millet, and sorghum
options.C: Processed wheat and refined sugar
options.D: Temperate climate root vegetables

explanation: Spot on! Traditional Nigerian diets rely heavily on locally grown grains, tubers, and legumes that thrive right here in our climate.

question: Where does the reservoir fit in the chain of infection?

options.A: It provides the home and starting point for the infectious germ
options.B: It acts as the final portal of entry into the new host
options.C: It functions as the chemical agent used to sterilize instruments
options.D: It serves as the physical method of airborne transmission

explanation: The reservoir is always link number one—it's the cozy starting home where the germ hangs out before starting its journey.

question: If someone has a family history of anxiety, what role does a major life stressor play?

options.A: It only affects physical heart rate and blood pressure
options.B: It can act as a trigger that activates the underlying condition
options.C: It completely erases any chance of developing symptoms
options.D: It replaces the need for biological evaluation entirely

explanation: Think of the genetic tendency as a loaded gun, and severe stress as the trigger that pulls it.

question: Why is it clinically important to treat pain quickly in emergency care, beyond just making the patient comfortable?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will be discharged within two hours.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any surgical interventions.
options.C: It prevents harmful physiological stress responses like high blood pressure and rapid heart rate.
options.D: It stops all forms of internal bleeding instantly.

explanation: Exactly! Unmanaged pain sends the body into a stress overdrive, pushing up heart rate and blood pressure, which makes stabilizing an emergency patient much harder.

question: Why might someone feel dizzy or carsick if they try to read a book inside a moving car?

options.A: The eyes and the inner ear send conflicting signals to the brain.
options.B: The brainstem shuts down the vestibular nuclei temporarily.
options.C: The proprioceptors in the neck freeze from lack of movement.
options.D: The visual cortex stops receiving oxygen from the carotid arteries.

explanation: Motion sickness happens when your eyes say "I'm sitting still reading," but your inner ear says "We are moving fast!" Confusion leads to that dizzy feeling. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h7)

question: When did the World Health Organization (WHO) publish its first Model List of Essential Medicines?
explanation: Great try! The WHO put out this very first list back in 1977 to bring order, safety, and priority to global drug markets.

question: Which blood tests are most important to check before a paracentesis to prevent bleeding?

options.A: Serum creatinine and BUN
options.B: Fasting blood glucose level
options.C: Coagulation profile and platelets
options.D: Total white blood cell count

explanation: We always check clotting times and platelets first to make sure the patient won't bleed too much from the needle poke.

question: Where are the internal female reproductive organs primarily located?

options.A: Inside the abdominal cavity
options.B: Within the true pelvis
options.C: Within the perineal body
options.D: Along the lower spinal canal

explanation: These organs are housed securely inside the bony true pelvis, which protects them from external trauma. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the main law protecting the rights of children in Nigeria?

options.A: The Adult Criminal Code
options.B: The Child Rights Act
options.C: The Public Land Decree
options.D: The National Health Insurance Act

explanation: Spot on! The Child Rights Act is the key legal framework safeguarding the welfare and special protection of minors in Nigeria.

question: What is the primary significance of traditional West African medicine in modern pharmacology?

options.A: It focuses solely on spiritual healing without any physical remedies.
options.B: Modern researchers isolate active chemical compounds from plants used by indigenous healers.
options.C: It provides cheap synthetic drugs for rural Nigerian clinics.
options.D: It has completely replaced the need for synthetic antibiotics in hospitals.

explanation: Many modern drugs are developed by studying the plants that traditional healers have successfully used for centuries to treat common ailments. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is proper post-harvest management important for food security?

options.A: It increases the chemical fertilizer content in staple grains
options.B: It removes the need for farmers to rotate their crops
options.C: It forces farmers to sell all their crops immediately after harvesting
options.D: It prevents food loss from pests and spoilage during lean periods

explanation: Correct! Storing and preserving food properly keeps it safe from pests so families have something to eat even when crops are scarce.

question: What is the primary role of research data in nursing?

options.A: Complicating routine patient documentation tasks
options.B: Replacing the clinical judgment of experienced nurses
options.C: Reducing the total number of required hospital staff
options.D: Providing a foundation for evidence-based practice

explanation: Research data gives nurses the solid proof needed to choose the safest, most effective care methods. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to getting accurate data on a busy ward?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully automated digital tools
options.B: Incomplete record-keeping in traditional paper registers
options.C: Heavy workloads and severe shortages of nursing personnel
options.D: Fear of punishment among staff when reporting clinical errors

explanation: We wish we had too much tech! In reality, staff shortages, paper logs, and fear of getting in trouble are the real hurdles—not having an overload of digital tools.

question: Why can myocarditis lead to signs of heart failure?

options.A: Heart valves become completely stuck open by fibrous scar tissue.
options.B: Electrical impulses travel too fast through the damaged heart chambers.
options.C: Inflammation damages the heart muscle cells, reducing their ability to contract effectively.
options.D: Fluid builds up inside the pericardial sac and crushes the coronary arteries.

explanation: When the heart muscle (myocardium) is inflamed, it gets tired and weak, losing its strong pumping power. This causes blood to back up—leading to heart failure symptoms.

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing blood vessel walls during pregnancy?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Think of progesterone as the great relaxer of smooth muscles in the body. It helps the body adapt to pregnancy, but it also relaxes vein walls, making them stretch out easily.

question: When a doctor prescribes medication for a child's conduct disorder, what is the main purpose?

question: Which photoreceptor cells in the retina are responsible for sharp color vision in bright light?

question: What is the primary purpose of follow-up care in mental health?

question: What do we call a live, real-time tele-nursing session?

question: Which of these research questions is best answered with a quantitative design?

question: Why shouldn't nurses just give anti-malarials immediately to every patient with a fever without testing first?

question: Which of the following is a direct surveillance responsibility for a clinical nurse?

options.D: Reporting suspected cases of priority diseases immediately

question: When should you change your basin water and washcloth during a bed bath?

question: What important health protection do hormonal contraceptives fail to provide that you must always emphasize to clients?

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual production of milk in the alveoli?

question: Which pain scale is best to use for a baby or toddler who cannot speak yet?

options.A: Wong-Baker FACES scale

options.D: Numeric Rating Scale

question: Which quick screening tool do healthcare workers use to check for problem drinking?

options.A: Braden scale
options.B: Apgar score chart
options.C: CAGE questionnaire
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

question: Which neurotransmitter is most directly linked to the brain's reward pathway and addiction?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Histamine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Dopamine is the primary chemical messenger responsible for reinforcing rewarding experiences in the brain's reward center. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why do nurses care so much about spotting workplace hazards early?

options.A: It stops short-term injuries and long-term chronic illnesses
options.B: It guarantees higher daily wages for industrial workers
options.C: It removes the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: It completely eliminates all physical labor in factories

explanation: Catching risks early means we can protect workers before they get seriously hurt. Prevention is always better than cure!

question: What is the most common trigger for a vaso-occlusive pain crisis in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Taking daily folic acid supplements

options.D: Sleeping on a firm mattress

question: What is the primary purpose of a research instrument in nursing studies?

question: What type of language works best when communicating with an autistic patient?

options.A: Jokes and light sarcasm

options.D: Clear and literal language

question: Which of these is a non-living place where germs can hang out and multiply?

options.A: A stray dog with rabies

options.D: A patient recovering from malaria

question: As a nurse, what crucial counseling point must you share with a client choosing natural family planning?

options.A: The calendar method works best for women with unpredictable cycles
options.B: Basal body temperature can replace barrier methods for infection control
options.C: These methods do not protect against sexually transmitted infections

question: A mum at 28 weeks comes to the clinic with swollen face and high blood pressure. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The fetus is growing at an unusually rapid and healthy rate
options.B: The mother is simply eating too much salt in her daily diet
options.C: This is a completely normal physical change in the third trimester
options.D: These are potential warning signs of preeclampsia requiring prompt evaluation

explanation: You nailed it! Sudden facial swelling plus high BP are red flags for preeclampsia. We always check these out immediately to keep the mum safe.

question: A patient can no longer feel hot or cold water on their foot after a back injury. Which pathway is likely affected?

options.A: Corticospinal tract

options.C: Cauda equina
options.D: Ventral root

question: What is the primary purpose of a policy brief?

question: Why should community health nurses team up with traditional birth attendants and local leaders?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from rural households

question: Why do nurses focus on empowerment in Family Life Education?

options.A: It forces community members to adopt identical lifestyles
options.B: It ensures that nurses make all final decisions for clients
options.C: It helps learners build critical thinking for better choices
options.D: It prevents individuals from questioning health policies

explanation: Empowerment means giving people the tools to think for themselves so they can make the best health decisions for their own lives.

question: Why do regular smokers need to smoke more over time to feel the same buzz?

options.A: Their lungs have expanded and require more volume
options.B: Their social circles encourage heavier smoking habits

options.D: The tobacco companies put weaker ingredients in newer packs

question: Why is it a mistake for nurses to rely only on hospital admission records when assessing community mental health needs?

question: Which of the following measurements is considered an anthropometric assessment tool?

question: What is the main goal of filing an incident report after a medication mistake?

options.A: To collect financial fines from the pharmacy department

options.D: To ensure the responsible nurse gets fired immediately

explanation: Incident reports aren't about blame—they help the team figure out what went wrong in the workflow so we can fix it and protect future patients.

question: A doctor updates a patient's drug dose on the computer, and you see it instantly on your clinical dashboard. Why is this real-time update so great?

question: How did the invention of psychotropic drugs change the daily job of a psychiatric nurse?

question: When a patient suddenly stands up and feels dizzy from a drop in blood pressure, how does the body normally respond?

question: An ICU patient is fighting the mechanical ventilator despite heavy sedation. What is the team likely to do next?

question: What is performance-based financing in healthcare?

question: Why do doctors often order a transvaginal ultrasound when a patient has abnormal bleeding?

question: Why is it helpful to know the boundaries of a healthcare system?

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's nutrition?

question: What is an immediate nursing action when critical lab results come back from the lab?

question: What is a major result of having very strict, restrictive abortion laws in a country?

question: A patient has a stiff, painful knee joint. Which membrane inside the joint is likely failing to produce enough lubricating fluid?

question: A clinic nurse notices a sudden spike in measles cases in the monthly records. What is the best practical step to take?

question: Why do milk-borne disease outbreaks often hit many people in a neighborhood all at once?

question: What is the main use of a urinal in the ward?

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to understand basic cell biology when giving medications?

question: What is the main goal of the health team concept in patient care?

question: Which nursing action best helps a patient who is trying to overcome avoidance behaviors triggered by anxiety?

question: What is the main purpose of filling out an incident report?

question: Why is having clear roles important for a healthcare team?

options.B: It ensures that doctors never have to touch a patient

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a person feel before taking health action?

question: What serious condition is strongly suspected when you see severe, locked Grade 3 moulding during labour?

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety practices?
